sentences.sentence: The study evaluated a 8-week multi-component digital literacy and digital wellbeing program for adolescents.
Its first aim was to test whether the program group showed more favorable pre-to-post changes in PIU, DSE and DGI than a wait-list control group.
Its second aim was to test whether post-intervention data were statistically consistent with a serial indirect association linking intervention condition, DSE, DGI and PIU.
A two-arm, parallel-group pretest-posttest quasi-experiment ran in March and April 2026 at a community center in Hubei Province, China.
It involved 206 adolescents aged 12–17, allocated by a quota-based procedure to intervention (n = 103) or wait-list control (n = 103).
Self-report measures were SPIUT (PIU), the AIAS Internet Self-Efficacy subscale (DSE) and the short DGI, all with established reliability.
Analysis used 2 × 2 repeated-measures ANOVA and PROCESS Model 6 serial mediation with 5,000 bootstrap samples.
The I-PACE model was used to inform the intervention logic.
The DSE → DGI → PIU sequence is described as theory-informed, yet "a theoretical proposition rather than an established causal mechanism".
Group × Time interactions were significant for PIU, F(1, 204) = 13.75, p < 0.001, ηp² = 0.063; DGI, F(1, 204) = 26.53, p < 0.001, ηp² = 0.115; and DSE, F(1, 204) = 18.62, p < 0.001, ηp² = 0.084.
In the wait-list group, DGI (p = 0.176) and DSE (p = 0.655) changes were not significant, while PIU decreased (p < 0.001).
The serial indirect path via DSE and DGI was significant, B = −2.589, 95% CI [−3.729, −1.575]; the single-mediator paths were not.
The authors conclude that participation was "associated with more favorable changes" in PIU, DSE and DGI than a wait-list condition.

The mediation results were statistically consistent with the DSE → DGI → PIU pathway, but alternative specifications indicated DGI had the more consistent association with PIU and did not establish temporal ordering.
They call the findings preliminary and hypothesis-generating, citing non-random allocation, concurrent measurement, self-report outcomes a single province and a short follow-up.

introduction: The first aim was to examine whether adolescents who received the program showed more favorable pre-to-post changes in PIU, DSE, and DGI than adolescents in a wait-list control group.
The second aim was to examine whether the post-intervention data were statistically consistent with a theory-informed serial indirect association linking intervention condition, DSE, DGI, and PIU.
the present study evaluated a 6-week multi-component digital literacy and digital wellbeing program for adolescents using a two-arm pretest-posttest quasi-experimental design.
methodology: A two-arm, parallel-group quasi-experimental design with pretest and posttest assessments was employed.
The study was conducted in March and April 2026 and was delivered in person at a community center in Hubei Province, China
Participants were 206 adolescents recruited from Hubei Province, China, through online advertisements disseminated via Wenjuanxing and community communication channels.
A total of 246 adolescents were assessed for eligibility through online screening.
allocated into intervention ( n = 103) and wait-list control ( n = 103) groups using a quota-based procedure
Problematic Internet use was measured using the Short Problematic Internet Use Test (SPIUT; Siciliano et al., 2015).
The Internet Self-Efficacy subscale of the Adolescent Internet Adaptability Scale (AIAS; Wang et al., 2025) was employed for assessing digital self-efficacy.
Delay of gratification was measured using the short-form Delaying Gratification Inventory (DGI; Hoerger et al., 2011).
The primary intervention analysis was conducted using 2 × 2 repeated-measures ANOVA, where group was a between-subjects factor whereas time was a within-subjects factor.
Hayes’ PROCESS macro, Model 6 was adopted for testing the mediation model
Bias-corrected bootstrap confidence intervals were used to test indirect effects based on 5,000 resamples.
theory: The Interaction of Person–Affect–Cognition–Execution (I-PACE) model was used to inform the overall intervention logic.
However, this sequence remains a theoretical proposition rather than an established causal mechanism.
These findings provide a theoretical basis for the proposed DSE → DGI → PIU sequence.
results: significant Group × Time interactions were observed for PIU, F (1, 204) = 13.75, p < 0.001, ηp 2 = 0.063; DGI, F (1, 204) = 26.53, p < 0.001, ηp 2 = 0.115; and DSE, F (1, 204) = 18.62, p < 0.001, ηp2 = 0.084.
whereas the change in the wait-list control group was not statistically significant, from 30.12 ± 2.23 to 31.58 ± 10.68, t (102) = −1.36, p = 0.176
whereas the wait-list control group showed no significant change, from 19.03 ± 6.10 to 18.62 ± 5.95, t (102) = 0.45, p = 0.655
only the sequential path from intervention condition to DSEpost, then to DGIpost, and finally to PIUpost was significant, B = −2.589, 95% CI [−3.729, −1.675].
The two single-mediator paths showed no significance since zero was involved in their CIs.
discussion: participation in a 6-week multi-component digital literacy and digital wellbeing program was associated with more favorable self-reported changes in problematic Internet use, digital self-efficacy, and delay of gratification than a wait-list condition.

The post-intervention data were statistically consistent with the hypothesized DSE → DGI → PIU indirect pathway, but alternative specifications indicated that DGI showed the more consistent association with PIU and did not establish temporal ordering.
The findings are therefore preliminary and hypothesis-generating.
First, participants were not randomly assigned to conditions.
Third, DSE, DGI, and PIU were measured concurrently at posttest.
Fourth, all primary outcomes were self-reported.
